sourceSentences: [0] I am kind of like going into his range and then stepping back to bait out the W. And so as soon as Alistar pops out, I instantly cue him here and then we are able to cancel him.
[0] Allistar knows that as soon as I get into W range, he's going to hold his W. So now it becomes a thing of like, okay, now we're just kind of like waiting who throws out what ability first.
[0] Charging your Q towards the direction the enemy is walking away so you can get a longer knockup
[1] I just need to hold my Q here for when Riven goes in. I do not poke with Q here. Riven is 100% marking my Q. She's just waiting for me to use it randomly for like poke or something.
[2] Her tornado stays in place when charging. Enemies can easily see the nado or hear the sound queue and simply just disengage.
[2] My best tips to avoid a Janna tornado is to simply reposition to the opposite of the lane or try to walk somewhere a bit less predictable.
[2] Since the tornado moves faster at full charge, it's a lot harder to dodge and also knocks up the enemy for a decent amount of time.
[2] Number five, expensive mana cost. If the stakes are higher and you know you only have a couple tornadoes before you run out of mana, the importance of hitting those tornadoes skyrockets.

[2] Wait for abilities to interrupt. Often, when champions are charging up a cast or channeling an ability, they are reducing their own movement speed. it's actually a golden opportunity for you to land your tornado anyway as they are less mobile.
[2] These enemies are waiting for you to tornado and for it to be on cooldown before they engage.
